newsitem.title: UK: Norilsk Nickel hopes for level-1 ADR issue.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nickel hopes for level-1 ADR issue.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group hopes to issue level-one American Depositary Receipts by July, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"By the end of the first half of this year (by July), we may issue level-one ADRs," Yuri Kaluzhsky, head of the group's projects and corporate finance section, told Reuters in an interview during the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's annual meeting. He did not say whether RAO Norilsky Nikel had received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for the ADR issues.
Kaluzhsky said the issue would be a private placement issued under SEC rule 144a and that Norilsk was in talks with Bank of New York on custodial matters.
Norilsk, based north of the Arctic Circle, is one of the world's leading producers of nickel, platinum, palladium and other metals.
ADRs are share look-alikes which allow stock in companies to be traded on foreign markets and which ease custody and settlement problems common in developing and emerging markets.
The SEC must conduct a thorough review of a company's accounts before granting permission for an ADR issue.
Level-one ADR issues are backed by existing company shares and do not raise any new capital or involve any issues of new shares.
Many Russian companies have issued or announced plans to issue ADRs. Shares of Russian companies which announce plans to issue ADRs generally outperform the market in the short-term.
Norilsk ordinaries had risen to $5.44 at around 1205 GMT on the Russian Trading System after Monday's close of $5.00.
